annotations: The phone runs no daemon and holds no code. It exists to answer the one question a machine cannot answer for you, which is whether a command may run. Every screen here is built around that.
The five screens the product exists for
The gate owns the screen rather than sitting in a thread. One primary decision at full width, the two alternatives beneath it.
Watching, and the shell is elsewhere
A refusal on a phone is the strongest version of the promise: the buttons are absent because the answer is not yours to give.
The app opens with no machine behind it, and says why
Launch names what is happening rather than spinning, and the mark carries its working variant while daemons answer.
The reason the list is empty is the architecture, so the copy says that rather than apologising.
One screen owns pairing. The others say plainly what they cannot show and why, instead of going blank.
The viewfinder states what it is looking for, and the typed path stays available rather than being buried.
Empty is not failure. The fleet is healthy and idle, so the screen says so and offers the two ways to start.
Reading the thread, typing into it, and attaching what the agent needs
The composer carries one plan button, tinted while a step needs you. Tapping it opens the rendered plan.
The keyboard takes the bottom half, the composer rides just above it, and the tab bar is gone while the field has focus.
Images are the settled scope, so the lower three sources are dimmed and say what each one waits on. Every source names where the bytes go, and nothing is stored on the phone.
Attachments grow the composer into a card, each thumb removable, and the size line says where the bytes go before you send. Images only, at the bound the annotation path already uses.
The plan, a design-studio render, and commenting on it from a phone
The plan is a document, not a status line. Each step carries its own state, and an edit says when it takes effect.
The same PLAN.md the desktop renders, read as a document. Headings, lists, code and checkboxes. The phone renders it and does not offer a raw view.
Choosing which variant the agent builds on happens at a desktop. A comment is a note; a choice is a commitment.
Full fidelity, not a status readout, in the same floating card the gate uses. Variants switch for viewing; choosing which one the agent builds on is desktop work.
Tap the bubble on an element, then write. The comment travels as coordinates plus text, never as a flattened screenshot.
Tapping the strip lifts the whole plan as a sheet. The thread stays behind it, so you have not left the conversation.
Four at once, so no progress bar

Needs you is the first group and it is never collapsed. Running subagents hang off their session on tree lines, and finished ones fold into one line. The line above it is M1's limit: without the relay there is no push, so gates arrive only while the app is open.
Tap a subagent under its session to read its thread. It is read-only here: a subagent takes instructions from claude-code, and its gates arrive in the parent thread.
Read-only. The receipt names the checkpoint the daemon took before the write, and reverting to it happens on a desktop.

Read-only. The view names the one device that holds the claim. Recent output arrives first, then live, redacted as everywhere else. The claimant's 120 columns wrap here, because a phone never resizes them. B in the thread opens it, and back returns there.
Extends 04. A phone or tablet reads the shell, and only the device holding the claim types into it
A gate after a failed command
The gate names the failed command it answers to and links to that output, read-only. The failure is red and the link is neutral, because amber belongs to the gate alone.
The same read-only view opens beside the thread at about 100 columns, so a 120-column line still wraps. A keyboard attached to the tablet does not type into it. The claimant still does.
The grant line, when this ships
One line, one source. It moves from a limit to a grant and names its limit in the same breath, and the desktop card, the command line and the phone change together.
A OR B, LONG LINES AT PHONE WIDTH
The same 14 lines of output, cropped to the phone's content width
Full screen gives about 52 columns. A long line wraps under a hanging indent, so a path or an assertion stays whole and the next line still starts at the margin.
Inside the thread the block is about 46 columns and seven lines tall. Sideways scrolling inside a scrolling thread fights the page, so it wraps and shows the tail.
B is the way in, A is where you read. Once long lines wrap, a seven-line block holds little more than the summary, so B shows the tail and one tap opens A.
Frame 04 is A. B is the thread block that opens it.
New literal strings for the conformance inventory, and what is not decided
Nothing can wake a phone over a tailnet, so the limit ships inside the success card. You learn when a gate can reach you at the moment you pair, not when one is missed.
A setting that does not exist yet stays listed, dimmed and untouchable, with no chevron. The line under it says why, so the missing row reads as a fact rather than a bug.
Attaches, then blocks send until removed.
Queued images the model cannot take lock send before you press it, and the line names the model. The 1.5 MB, 2048 px and count caps are unchanged.
WHEN A GATE CAN REACH THIS PHONE
Three versions of the line, at phone width, dark and light
One payload rule: a push says that something happened, never what. Push needs the hosted relay and accounts, so all of this ships after the first release.
Facts do not fit, so only Open
Rule: if one fact would be cut, the lock screen cannot decide. Nine paths do not fit the expanded notification, so Open is the only action and every path waits in the app.

Rule: a stale notification decides nothing. An answer from another device replaces the notification, and the daemon keeps only the first answer. An expired handle fetches no facts, and the gate keeps waiting on its machine.
Rule: the roster carries the same payload as 21, nothing more. Four sessions share no denominator, so there is no combined progress bar.
What the collapsed notification could say. Bodies are encrypted to the phone. On iOS a Live Activity cannot decrypt, so 21 to 23 stay at A there.
